lines.meet: I'm Tobias, a paladin and a stonemason. Mind the scaffold, please, and don't lean on that wall yet.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're at Light's Hope as well, I think. I'm the one on the scaffold by the chapel wall, Tobias.
lines.ask_home: Where's home for you? Mine had a cathedral in it, so you'll have to compete.
lines.ask_work: Your hands have calluses in odd places. What work put them there?
lines.answer_home: Bonn, where my father was a carpenter, and then sixteen years in Cologne.
lines.answer_work: Stonemason on the Cologne Cathedral works crew. It's been under repair for seven hundred years, and it'll never be finished.
lines.chat_food: Kölsch with the crew after a shift, in the little glasses, and a Halve Hahn, which isn't half a chicken at all. It's a cheese roll.
lines.chat_sleep: I go to bed early and sleep like stone, after a day of carrying it.
lines.chat_missing: The cathedral bells at noon, from up on the roof, so loud you feel them in your teeth.
lines.chat_here: The Light came to me slowly, the way good mortar sets. Now it holds, and I don't think about it much.
lines.tease_quiet: We could work a whole shift together, {name}, and say nothing but pass the trowel. I'd call that a fine day's work.
lines.tease_talker: You'd talk the mortar dry before it set, {name}.
lines.tease_careful: You measure twice, {name}, like a proper mason. The cathedral would have you.
lines.tease_bold: You'd climb the scaffold before the boards were tied, {name}. Please, not on my wall.
lines.tease_any: You'd be a fine gargoyle, {name}, if you held that expression a few hundred years.
lines.tease_back: Na ja, {name}, that was well laid. I'll give you that.
lines.take_it_kindly: Na ja, that's fair, {name}. I can't argue with good work.
lines.bristle: Some things I don't joke about, {name}, and that's one of them.
lines.apologise: That was shoddy of me, and I'm sorry. I'll put it right.
lines.double_down: I don't say much, so when I do, I mean it. I'm keeping that one.
lines.needle_quiet: You saw the crack and didn't say. A crack you don't mention is how a wall comes down.
lines.needle_talker: Please, a little quiet. You can't hear stone settle if you're talking over it.
lines.needle_careful: You've been at it so long the mortar's gone off. Lay the stone, please.
lines.needle_bold: You lean on walls before the mortar's set, every time. One day one of them will lean back.
lines.needle_any: Your work is shoddy, and you know it, and you leave it anyway.
lines.bite_back: I've held the front of this party for months without giving an inch. Think again before you say that.
lines.hurt: That cracked something, I think. I'll be up on the scaffold a while.
lines.laugh_off: Seven hundred years of masons have been called worse by their bishops. I'll survive it.
lines.confide: {name}, I never married. There were twelve of us on the crew, and we ate lunch on the cathedral roof every day, and they were more family to me than anyone.
lines.listen: Sit, {name}, I'm not going anywhere. Say it slowly, and I'll hold it.
lines.look_out: Keep to the left of me, {name}. Whatever comes will hit me first.
lines.accept: Na ja, {name}, if you say so. I'll be careful.
lines.deflect: It's a scratch, {name}, nothing more. Stone's done worse to me.
lines.check_in: Steady, {name}, slowly now. Where did it hit you?
lines.blame: Somebody leaned on a wall that wasn't ready in there, and we all came down with it.
lines.thank: Thank you. I felt myself going, and you held me up like good scaffolding.
lines.brush_off: You were falling and I was there, that's all. Rest a moment.
lines.worry: That was much too close, {name}. Sit, and don't lean on anything.
lines.handed_down: Your gear's come to me, it seems. Mortar gets on everything, but I'll do my best.
lines.hand_fine: Keep it, keep it. I've my chisel, and that's all a mason needs.
lines.hand_sulk: A word first would have been good, that's all.
lines.turn_friendly: You can stand on my scaffold any time, {name}. I'll tie the boards for you.
lines.turn_friends: When I build something here that lasts, {name}, I'll want you to see it first.
lines.turn_grating: We don't set well together, I think, like bad mortar. Na ja, it happens.
lines.turn_rivals: Whatever comes at us, it'll hit me before it hits you. That's the job, not a kindness.
lines.make_up: Na ja, {name}, enough. Let's lay this one again, properly.
lines.defend: No, that isn't true, I was watching. Let {name} alone.
lines.friend_left: The scaffold's quiet without {name}. I keep turning to pass the trowel.
lines.friend_back: Ah, {name}, good, you're back on the scaffold.
lines.common_stone: You know stone, I've watched you touch a wall. Anybody who's worked it knows it remembers every hand that set it.
lines.common_music: You sing, don't you? I've heard you humming low. I've started a choir, and there's always room for one more voice.
